_note: English version (?lang=en). t = what the voice says (figures written as words so the lips follow them); sub = the subtitle when it differs; en = the English subtitle; to / glance as in lines.ar.json. Voices: python -I tools/gen_voice.py en.

nar_open.t: The company's research points to a service gap. The proposal: extra labor hours in the stores, at a cost of about forty million dollars a year. Will that money come back? Nobody knows yet.
nar_open.en: The company's research points to a service gap. The proposal: extra labor hours in the stores, at a cost of about forty million dollars a year. Will that money come back? Nobody knows yet.

priya_hello.t: Good evening. Before we decide on the forty million, Noor has brought us a recording of the store itself.
priya_hello.en: Good evening. Before we decide on the forty million, Noor has brought us a recording of the store itself.

noor_model.t: This is the Al-Midan store as we recorded it on Tuesday morning, minute by minute. Everyone you see on the screen was really there. Look at the counter.
noor_model.en: This is the Al-Midan store as we recorded it on Tuesday morning, minute by minute. Everyone you see on the screen was really there. Look at the counter.

noor_spec.t: The queue looks long now. Pull up the slower and quieter periods before we decide what to change.
noor_spec.en: The queue looks long now. Pull up the slower and quieter periods before we decide what to change.

noor_s2.t: Same store, same staff. Only the hour is different.
noor_s2.en: Same store, same staff. Only the hour is different.

noor_cards.t: And these are two comments from the comment box that day.
noor_cards.en: And these are two comments from the comment box that day.

noor_rail.t: The register isn't the problem. It's the drink that's slow.
noor_rail.en: The register isn't the problem. It's the drink that's slow.

noor_q.t: Which service problem would you investigate first?
noor_q.en: Which service problem would you investigate first?

noor_h_peak.t: That's what your numbers say. Let's see what fixing it costs.
noor_h_peak.en: That's what your numbers say. Let's see what fixing it costs.

noor_h_acc.t: The comment described accuracy positively. What other accuracy evidence would you want?
noor_h_acc.en: The comment described accuracy positively. What other accuracy evidence would you want?

noor_h_all.t: Peak and off-peak are different. Which period would you measure again?
noor_h_all.en: Peak and off-peak are different. Which period would you measure again?

ellis_open.t: A shorter line helps the customer. But my question is: how many extra completed orders do we need each day to cover the new labor?
ellis_open.en: A shorter line helps the customer. But my question is: how many extra completed orders do we need each day to cover the new labor?

ellis_scale.t: This pan holds the added labor for a year; that one, what the extra orders add. The pale figures outside the door on the screen are an assumption — nobody has seen them yet.
ellis_scale.en: This pan holds the added labor for a year; that one, what the extra orders add. The pale figures outside the door on the screen are an assumption — nobody has seen them yet.

ellis_coins.t: Put a coin in the orders’ pan for every extra completed order a day, until the pans balance.
ellis_coins.en: Put a coin in the orders’ pan for every extra completed order a day, until the pans balance.

ellis_level.t: Level. Twenty extra orders a day cover the labor — if each order adds three dollars.
ellis_level.en: Level. Twenty extra orders a day cover the labor — if each order adds three dollars.

ellis_play.t: Try the assumptions yourself. Move the numbers and compare.
ellis_play.en: Try the assumptions yourself. Move the numbers and compare.

ellis_12.t: At twelve orders we lose eight thousand six hundred and forty dollars a year at this store.
ellis_12.sub: At 12 orders we lose $8,640 a year at this store.
ellis_12.en: At 12 orders we lose $8,640 a year at this store.

ellis_26.t: We make six thousand four hundred and eighty dollars. Fourteen orders a day is all that separates a loss from a profit.
ellis_26.sub: We make $6,480. Fourteen orders a day is all that separates a loss from a profit.
ellis_26.en: We make $6,480. Fourteen orders a day is all that separates a loss from a profit.

ellis_25.t: Notice the break-even moved to twenty-four orders. A small assumption changes the decision.
ellis_25.sub: Notice the break-even moved to 24 orders. A small assumption changes the decision.
ellis_25.en: Notice the break-even moved to 24 orders. A small assumption changes the decision.

ellis_contrib.t: Notice how the break-even moved when the profit per order changed. A small assumption changes the decision.
ellis_contrib.en: Notice how the break-even moved when the profit per order changed. A small assumption changes the decision.

ellis_done.t: All right, Priya — the numbers are in front of you now.
ellis_done.en: All right, Priya — the numbers are in front of you now.

priya_open.t: We need a recommendation today. What would make you keep it — or reverse it?
priya_open.en: We need a recommendation today. What would make you keep it — or reverse it?

p_rec_all.t: I recommend adding staff across all stores now.
p_rec_all.en: I recommend adding staff across all stores now.

p_rec_pilot.t: I recommend a matched-store pilot first.
p_rec_pilot.en: I recommend a matched-store pilot first.

p_rec_handoff.t: I recommend keeping staffing steady and testing the pickup step first.
p_rec_handoff.en: I recommend keeping staffing steady and testing the pickup step first.

noor_c_all.t: I can have every store's schedule ready from next week.
noor_c_all.en: I can have every store's schedule ready from next week.

ellis_c_all.t: If the lift comes in lower than we hope, we lose money in every store.
ellis_c_all.en: If the lift comes in lower than we hope, we lose money in every store.

ellis_c_pilot.t: Same weeks, same peak hours. That's how we know the difference came from the labor.
ellis_c_pilot.en: Same weeks, same peak hours. That's how we know the difference came from the labor.

noor_c_handoff.t: I'll try a simpler handoff at the shelf in one store, before any hiring.
noor_c_handoff.en: I'll try a simpler handoff at the shelf in one store, before any hiring.

priya_match.t: That's a condition I can review in two months.
priya_match.en: That's a condition I can review in two months.

priya_other.t: It's a good condition, but it doesn't test the decision you made.
priya_other.en: It's a good condition, but it doesn't test the decision you made.

priya_feel.t: A feeling isn't a measurement. What exactly will you measure?
priya_feel.en: A feeling isn't a measurement. What exactly will you measure?

priya_close.t: Thank you. I have the memo.
priya_close.en: Thank you. I have the memo.

nar_end.t: The published case asks managers to weigh service improvement against a forty-million-dollar yearly labor commitment. The store model you explored showed how the whole decision shifts when the order volume shifts.
nar_end.en: The published case asks managers to weigh service improvement against a forty-million-dollar yearly labor commitment. The store model you explored showed how the whole decision shifts when the order volume shifts.
